source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_original: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras / dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_english: From this they fear and desire, they grieve and rejoice, and do not discern the air, shut in by darkness and a blind prison.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: unde et illud Uergilianum est: hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque neque auras dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
reuse.text_original: unde et illud Uergilianum est: hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque neque auras dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
reuse.text_english: Whence also that line of Vergil comes: from here they fear and desire, they grieve and rejoice, and, shut up in darkness and blind prison, they do not discern the light of day.
